Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration had no causal effect on depressive symptoms.
Sentence: "MR analysis revealed no causal effects of 25(OH)vitamin D concentration, either on DS (inverse variance weighted (IVW); b = 0.025, SE = 0.038, p = 0.52) or on BD (IVW; b = 0.020, SE = 0.012, p = 0.10)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (DS)
Population: Genetic summary data: 161,460 participants for depressive symptoms GWAS; SUNLIGHT GWAS of 79,366 subjects for 25(OH)D instruments
Intervention: Genetically predicted 25(OH)vitamin D concentration (six SNPs)
Comparator: None (Mendelian randomization)
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 322,280
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Older adults deficient in vitamin D had higher odds of depressive symptoms than those with sufficient vitamin D, after adjustment.
Sentence: "The crude analysis showed that vitamin D deficient participants had 3.08 (CI = 1.53;6.20) times higher odds to present depressive symptoms compared to vitamin D sufficiency."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (15-item Geriatric Depression Scale)
Population: Community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and over from southern Brazil (EpiFloripa Aging Study)
Intervention: Serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol deficiency (≤20 ng/mL), measured, not given
Comparator: Vitamin D sufficiency (≥30 ng/mL)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 557
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed
